events.title: The Trial of Joan of Arc Begins
events.description: In English-occupied Rouen, judges opened the preliminary investigations into Joan of Arc, the teenage military leader who had rallied French forces during the Hundred Years' War.
events.significance: The proceedings ended with her execution later that year. Her trial became one of history's most famous legal dramas, and she was later declared innocent and canonized.

events.title: Philip Astley Stages the First Modern Circus
events.description: In London, the cavalry veteran and horse trainer Philip Astley staged a show of trick riding in a ring. It is regarded as the first modern circus.
events.significance: Astley's ring format and mix of acts set the pattern for circuses around the world.

events.title: Connecticut Joins the Union
events.description: Connecticut ratified the United States Constitution and became the fifth state to enter the Union.
events.significance: Its ratification added momentum to the young nation's new federal government.

events.title: The Star of the West Is Fired Upon
events.description: As the civilian ship Star of the West tried to bring supplies and reinforcements to Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor, it was fired upon and forced to turn back.
events.significance: The incident came just before the American Civil War began and showed how close the country was to open conflict.

events.title: Steve Jobs Unveils the First iPhone
events.description: Apple co-founder Steve Jobs introduced the first iPhone, which combined a phone, an iPod and an internet device.
events.significance: The iPhone helped launch the modern smartphone era and changed how people communicate, work and get information.
